transcript:
[doctor] Hi Ms. Gonzalez, how are you today?

[patient] Hello, Doctor. I've been better, to be honest. I've been having this burning sensation when I urinate for the past few days.

[doctor] I'm sorry to hear that. Can you tell me a bit more about your symptoms?

[patient] Sure, it's been about 5 days now. It really burns when I go to the bathroom, and I feel like I need to go all the time. I've also been having some pain in my lower abdomen.

[doctor] I understand. Has this been affecting your sleep at all?

[patient] Yes, it has. I've only been getting about 4 to 5 hours of sleep a night because I wake up needing to go to the bathroom.

[doctor] That sounds really uncomfortable. Have you experienced any nausea, vomiting, or changes in your bowel habits?

[patient] No, none of those.

[doctor] Alright. Have you had these symptoms before?

[patient] Yes, I have a history of urinary tract infections. It seems like they keep coming back.

[doctor] I see. And you also have Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, correct?

[patient] Yes, that's right.

[doctor] When was your last UTI?

[patient] It was about three months ago.

[doctor] Okay, thank you for that information. Let me do a quick physical examination.

[patient] Alright.

[doctor] I see you are in no acute distress and are cooperative. Let me check your abdomen. Does it hurt when I press here?

[patient] Yes, that's tender.

[doctor] You have tenderness in your lower abdomen, specifically suprapubic tenderness. I'll also check your external genitalia. Everything looks normal here, no discharge or lesions.

[patient] Okay.

[doctor] I have ordered a urine culture and sensitivity test. We'll need to wait for those results, but based on your symptoms and history, it does sound like you have another UTI.

[patient] That makes sense. What can we do about it?

[doctor] I'm going to start you on Ciprofloxacin, 500 mg, orally, every 12 hours for 7 days. That's 14 tablets in total.

[patient] Okay, I can do that.

[doctor] I’ll also refer you for an ultrasound of the renal and bladder to rule out any structural abnormalities or presence of stones.

[patient] Is that necessary?

[doctor] Given your recurrent UTIs, it’s important to rule out any underlying issues. It’s just a precaution.

[patient] I understand.

[doctor] We'll also need to follow up in 2 weeks to reassess your symptoms and review the urine culture results.

[patient] Alright, I’ll make sure to come back.

[doctor] Now let’s talk about some lifestyle modifications. It’s crucial that you increase your water intake. Aim for at least 8 glasses of water per day.

[patient] I’ll try to drink more water.

[doctor] Good. I also want to discuss your diet. High carbohydrate intake and minimal physical activity can impact your diabetes and contribute to recurrent UTIs.

[patient] I know my diet isn’t great. I love my carbs.

[doctor] It’s important to monitor your blood glucose levels regularly and maintain optimal glycemic control. This can help prevent future UTIs.

[patient] I’ll do my best.

[doctor] Incorporating moderate physical activity into your routine can also make a big difference. Try to walk for at least 30 minutes a day.

[patient] I can try that. 

[doctor] Excellent. Do you have any questions about the treatment plan?

[patient] No, I think I understand everything.

[doctor] Great. Remember, if your symptoms worsen or you have any concerns, don’t hesitate to contact us.

[patient] I will. Thank you, Doctor.

[doctor] You're welcome, Ms. Gonzalez. Take care and see you in 2 weeks.

[patient] Thank you. Bye.
